title: 4 Months of development on my Auto Battler 'Wizard Tournament'. Where I went wrong & where I went right:
author: RachopDev
selftext:
Video attached is a tiktok video of gameplay that did decent.   
  
I released my game July 29th on Steam. I have since sold 150 copies and 100 unique demo players.   
My biggest regret was simply being too excited. I should not have released my game as quickly as I did. In hindsight, when I originally released it I thought I was done.   
  
When I look at the game today I don't even recognize it from my released game, its so much better. And all that time I spent improving it, I could have been collecting Wish lists for a better launch.

I added a suggestion box in-game where people can type whatever and send it to my email. This was a gigantic boon for me. I got a ton of suggestions/bug reports etc coming through that little box I added.

All I'm trying to say is, please do not be trigger happy with your game. Let it sit, submit a demo to next fest. As soon as to you think the game is done, remind yourself its not. Having a stand out game in 2026 requires damn near perfection, especially when debuffed with AI disclosure.   


For those interested: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4917740/Wizard\_Tournament/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4917740/Wizard_Tournament/)  
Demo is practically the full game if you want to try it out. 

I don't want to make a text wall post so if you have any questions I'm happy to answer anything.

replies.author: RachopDev
replies.body:
I run Codex through Godot. I did a lot of the work on Sol-Medium and toward the end when I felt like everything was in place I moved to Astra-Very high. 

I purchased sprite packs from [Itch.io](http://Itch.io) for a total of about $30USD.

Sounds came from either open source libraries or [elevenlabs.io](http://elevenlabs.io) 

When it came to image generation, I replaced every asset before I even released, and then replaced them again post release. I ended up getting the best results by generating with GPT-Astra. Creating working bitmaps for intended image size use. Added edge softening and slight backdrop/outline shadow. Prompting with GPT was mostly just finding the perfect first image, and then using that to template the second image, then I use both to template the third and so on. 

I did also load most of my generated images into Photopea to clean edges, add pixels and remove artifacts. 

Game testing  was 90% done by my demo players and their feedback through the suggestion box. I also made the game for myself as much as I did the customers. I've got 60 hours played on steam which I consider testing. 

No interesting skills to share other than the advice to persevere and polish your polish.
